description: ralph_providers returns all enabled providers with filtered model lists
steps: Call ralph_providers MCP tool with no parameters
Verify response is valid JSON with 'providers', 'defaults', and 'summarizer' keys
Verify only enabled providers (both top-level and ralph.providers) are included
Verify each provider has 'name', 'display_name', and 'models' array
Verify models reflect allowlist/blocklist filtering from settings

description: ralph_providers respects per-model allowlist filtering
steps: Configure ralph.providers.claude.models = ['opus', 'sonnet'] in settings.json
Call ralph_providers
Verify claude provider's models array contains only 'opus' and 'sonnet'
Verify 'haiku' is NOT in the models array

description: ralph_providers respects per-model blocklist filtering
steps: Configure ralph.providers.opencode.models_blocked = ['openai/gpt-3.5-turbo'] in settings.json
Call ralph_providers
Verify opencode provider's models array does NOT contain 'openai/gpt-3.5-turbo'
Verify all other opencode models are present

description: ralph_providers returns defaults and summarizer config
steps: Configure ralph.defaults and ralph.summarizer in settings.json
Call ralph_providers
Verify defaults object has 'provider', 'model', 'iterations' fields matching settings
Verify summarizer object has 'provider', 'model' fields matching settings

description: ralph_providers handles missing CLI gracefully
steps: Enable opencode provider but ensure opencode CLI is not installed
Call ralph_providers
Verify opencode provider appears with empty models array
Verify no crash or exception - tool returns valid JSON

description: ralph_providers handles missing ralph settings section
steps: Remove the 'ralph' section from settings.json entirely
Call ralph_providers
Verify fallback to top-level providers with all models available
Verify default iterations = 3

description: ralph_start creates job directory and spawns subprocess for plan mode
steps: Call ralph_start with slug='test-plan', mode='plan', task_description='Test planning task'
Verify .vista/ralph/test-plan/ directory is created
Verify job.json exists with correct metadata (job_id, slug, mode, status, provider, model)
Verify task.md contains the task description
Verify PROMPT_plan.md is generated from template
Verify progress.txt is created
Verify response contains job_id and status='running'
Verify a subprocess was spawned (PID recorded in job.json)

description: ralph_start creates job directory and spawns subprocess for build mode
steps: Call ralph_start with slug='test-build', mode='build', task_description='Build task'
Verify .vista/ralph/test-build/ directory is created
Verify PROMPT_build.md is generated from template
Verify response contains job_id and status='running'

description: ralph_start uses default provider/model/iterations when not specified
steps: Configure defaults in settings.json (provider='claude', model='sonnet', iterations=3)
Call ralph_start with only slug, mode, and task_description (no provider/model/iterations)
Verify job.json shows provider='claude', model='sonnet', iterations=3
Verify subprocess was invoked with the default model

description: ralph_start accepts explicit provider/model/iterations parameters
steps: Call ralph_start with provider='claude', model='opus', iterations=5
Verify job.json shows provider='claude', model='opus', iterations=5
Verify subprocess was invoked with model='opus' and max iterations=5

description: ralph_start returns within 5 seconds
steps: Call ralph_start and measure response time
Verify response is received within 5 seconds
Verify subprocess is running independently (tool didn't wait for completion)

description: ralph_start rejects duplicate slug with active job
steps: Call ralph_start with slug='active-job' - succeeds
Call ralph_start again with slug='active-job' while first job is still running
Verify error response indicating slug already has an active job
Verify existing job_id is included in error response for reference

description: ralph_start allows reuse of slug with completed job
steps: Create and complete a job with slug='reuse-test'
Call ralph_start with slug='reuse-test' again
Verify new job is created with a new job_id
Verify previous job.json is preserved as job.{old-id}.json

description: ralph_start rejects invalid mode
steps: Call ralph_start with mode='invalid'
Verify error response indicating mode must be 'plan' or 'build'

description: ralph_start rejects unavailable provider
steps: Call ralph_start with provider='nonexistent'
Verify error response indicating provider is not enabled or not found

description: ralph_status returns lightweight progress for running job
steps: Start a job and let it begin running
Call ralph_status with the job_id
Verify response contains status='running', current_iteration, total_iterations
Verify response contains last few lines from progress.txt
Verify response contains elapsed_time

description: ralph_status detects completed job via PID check
steps: Start a job and wait for the subprocess to finish naturally
Call ralph_status with the job_id
Verify status is 'completed' (PID no longer alive, exit code 0)
Verify completed_at timestamp is set in job.json

description: ralph_status detects failed job via PID check
steps: Start a job with a configuration that will cause the subprocess to fail
Wait for the subprocess to exit with non-zero code
Call ralph_status with the job_id
Verify status is 'failed'
Verify error message is populated in response

description: ralph_status returns within 1 second
steps: Call ralph_status and measure response time
Verify response is received within 1 second
Verify no subprocess was spawned (lightweight operation)

description: ralph_status returns clear error for invalid job_id
steps: Call ralph_status with job_id='nonexistent-id'
Verify error response indicating job not found

description: ralph_summary returns AI-generated summary for completed job
steps: Complete a plan job that produced IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md and progress.txt
Call ralph_summary with the job_id
Verify response is valid JSON with status_summary, completed_work, issues, recommendations
Verify the summary reflects actual content from the job artifacts

description: ralph_summary works for in-progress (running) jobs
steps: Start a job and let it run for at least one iteration
Call ralph_summary while the job is still running
Verify summary reflects partial progress (in_progress list populated)
Verify no interference with the running loop subprocess

description: ralph_summary uses configured summarizer provider and model
steps: Configure ralph.summarizer.provider='claude' and ralph.summarizer.model='haiku'
Call ralph_summary for a completed job
Verify the summarizer subprocess was invoked with claude CLI and haiku model

description: ralph_summary truncates large artifacts before sending to summarizer
steps: Create a job with a very large progress.txt (1000+ lines)
Call ralph_summary
Verify progress.txt was truncated to last 100 lines in summarizer prompt
Verify IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md was truncated to first 500 lines

description: ralph_summary handles summarizer CLI not installed
steps: Configure summarizer with a provider whose CLI is not installed
Call ralph_summary
Verify clear error message indicating the CLI tool is not available

description: ralph_summary handles summarizer timeout
steps: Call ralph_summary for a job (summarizer configured to take very long)
Verify timeout after 55 seconds (within MCP 60s limit)
Verify subprocess is killed on timeout
Verify error response indicating timeout

description: ralph_summary handles malformed summarizer output
steps: Mock summarizer CLI to return non-JSON output
Call ralph_summary
Verify graceful fallback - raw text returned or best-effort parse

description: ralph_stop terminates running job subprocess
steps: Start a job and confirm it's running
Call ralph_stop with the job_id
Verify subprocess is terminated (PID no longer alive)
Verify job.json status updated to 'stopped'
Verify response confirms the stop

description: ralph_stop handles already-completed job gracefully
steps: Complete a job naturally
Call ralph_stop with the completed job's id
Verify response indicates job already completed (not an error, just informational)

description: ralph_stop handles invalid job_id
steps: Call ralph_stop with job_id='nonexistent'
Verify error response indicating job not found

description: Full plan+build lifecycle via MCP tools
steps: Call ralph_providers to discover available options
Call ralph_start with slug='lifecycle-test', mode='plan', provider and model from discovery
Poll ralph_status every 10 seconds until status is 'completed'
Call ralph_summary to get the plan summary
Verify plan artifacts exist (IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md, progress.txt)
Call ralph_start with same slug, mode='build'
Poll ralph_status until status is 'completed'
Call ralph_summary to get the build summary
Verify build artifacts exist and code changes were made

description: Settings filtering: both provider levels must be enabled
steps: Set top-level providers.opencode.enabled=true
Set ralph.providers.opencode.enabled=false
Call ralph_providers
Verify opencode is NOT in the returned providers list
Reverse: set top-level to false, ralph to true
Verify opencode is still NOT in the returned providers list

description: Settings filtering: allowlist takes precedence over blocklist
steps: Set ralph.providers.claude with both models=['opus'] and models_blocked=['haiku']
Call ralph_providers
Verify only 'opus' is returned (models allowlist wins)

description: Job state survives MCP server restart
steps: Start a ralph job
Restart the MCP server (kill and relaunch)
Call ralph_status with the original job_id
Verify status is correctly reported (running or completed depending on subprocess state)
Verify job metadata is intact from disk

description: Multiple concurrent ralph jobs run independently
steps: Call ralph_start with slug='job-a'
Call ralph_start with slug='job-b'
Verify both jobs are running (different PIDs)
Call ralph_status for each - both report independent progress
Stop job-a, verify job-b continues running

description: Dashboard API lists all ralph jobs
steps: Create 3 ralph jobs with different statuses (running, completed, failed)
GET /api/ralph/jobs
Verify response contains all 3 jobs with correct metadata
Verify jobs are sorted by creation time (newest first)

description: Dashboard API returns job detail
steps: Create a ralph job
GET /api/ralph/jobs/{job_id}
Verify response contains full job metadata
Verify progress content is included
Verify artifact file listing is included

description: Dashboard API returns progress.txt content
steps: Create a ralph job and let it produce progress output
GET /api/ralph/jobs/{job_id}/progress
Verify response contains progress.txt content
Verify content updates on subsequent requests as job progresses

description: Dashboard API lists and reads artifact files
steps: Complete a ralph job that produced multiple artifacts
GET /api/ralph/jobs/{job_id}/artifacts
Verify response lists all files in the job directory
GET /api/ralph/jobs/{job_id}/artifacts/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md
Verify response contains the file contents

description: Dashboard API can stop a running job
steps: Start a ralph job
POST /api/ralph/jobs/{job_id}/stop
Verify job status changes to 'stopped'
Verify subprocess is terminated

description: Dashboard API handles nonexistent job gracefully
steps: GET /api/ralph/jobs/nonexistent-id
Verify 404 response with clear error message

description: Dashboard job list view renders correctly in browser
steps: Create several ralph jobs with various statuses
Open Vista dashboard in browser
Navigate to ralph jobs section
Verify table shows slug, mode, provider, model, status, and timestamp for each job
Verify status indicators use correct colors (blue=running, green=completed, red=failed)

description: Dashboard job detail view shows progress and artifacts
steps: Create a running ralph job
Click on the job in the dashboard list
Verify job detail page shows job metadata
Verify progress section displays and auto-updates
Verify artifacts section lists clickable file links

description: ralph_start returns within MCP timeout with subprocess detached
steps: Call ralph_start 10 times with different slugs
Verify all 10 calls return within 5 seconds each
Verify no memory leaks from spawned subprocesses

description: ralph_status returns within 1 second even with large progress.txt
steps: Create a job with a 10,000-line progress.txt
Call ralph_status
Verify response within 1 second (only reads last N lines)

description: ralph_summary completes within MCP 60-second timeout
steps: Create a job with substantial artifacts
Call ralph_summary
Verify summarizer subprocess completes within 55 seconds
Verify total tool response within 60 seconds

description: No API keys are stored in job directories or settings
steps: Complete a full plan+build lifecycle
Inspect all files in .vista/ralph/{slug}/
Verify no API keys, tokens, or credentials are present in any file
Inspect vista/settings.json
Verify no API keys in settings (only provider names and model names)

description: Subprocess stdin is isolated from MCP stdin
steps: Start a ralph job
Verify subprocess uses stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL or subprocess.PIPE (not inherited)
Verify MCP server continues to function normally while subprocess runs

description: Prompt files use existing portable templates with ad-hoc context
steps: Call ralph_start with task_description='Refactor API handlers'
Read the generated PROMPT_plan.md in the job directory
Verify it follows the structure of vista/portable/templates/PROMPT_plan.md
Verify task.md reference is injected (agent looks for task.md instead of specs/)
Verify project root and feature directory paths are correct

description: Job directory structure matches specification
steps: Call ralph_start and let job complete
Verify .vista/ralph/{slug}/ contains: job.json, task.md, PROMPT_{mode}.md, progress.txt
Verify IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md is created by the worker (for plan mode)
Verify output.log captures subprocess stdout/stderr

description: Orphaned process detection on MCP server restart
steps: Start a ralph job
Kill the MCP server without stopping the job
Restart MCP server
Call ralph_status - verify it correctly detects the subprocess state
If subprocess still running: status shows 'running'
If subprocess exited: status shows 'completed' or 'failed' based on exit code

description: Windows platform PID checking works correctly
steps: Start a ralph job on Windows
Call ralph_status and verify PID check returns 'running'
Let job complete naturally
Call ralph_status and verify PID check detects process ended
Verify no Windows-specific errors in output.log

description: ralph_providers returns model metadata (cost_tier, best_for_tags, best_for_notes)
steps: Configure model_metadata for opus with cost_tier='expensive', best_for_tags=['complex reasoning']
Call ralph_providers
Verify each model object has 'cost_tier', 'best_for_tags', 'best_for_notes' fields
Verify opus model shows cost_tier='expensive' and correct tags
Verify models without metadata show null cost_tier and empty arrays

description: ralph_providers discovers models live from provider CLIs (not hardcoded)
steps: Call ralph_providers
Verify claude models come from ClaudeProvider.get_models() (same as ralph.py line 295)
Verify opencode models come from live 'opencode models' CLI call
Add a new model to opencode config, call ralph_providers again
Verify new model appears in response without any code changes

description: ralph_start uses same LOOP_SCRIPT_TEMPLATE and provider.get_invocation() as ralph.py
steps: Call ralph_start with provider='claude', model='opus'
Read the generated loop.ps1 in the job directory
Verify it matches the output of ralph.py's LOOP_SCRIPT_TEMPLATE.format() with same parameters
Verify the invocation block matches ClaudeProvider.get_invocation('ps1')
Verify PowerShell execution flags match ralph.py (ExecutionPolicy Bypass)

description: Settings UI page loads with live model discovery
steps: Navigate to /settings/ralph in browser
Verify page calls GET /api/settings/ralph which calls provider.get_models() live
Verify claude models table shows rows from ClaudeProvider.get_models()
Verify opencode models table shows rows from live 'opencode models' CLI
Verify model names are NOT hardcoded in the HTML template

description: Settings UI shows provider enable/disable toggles
steps: Navigate to /settings/ralph
Verify each provider has an enable/disable checkbox
Toggle opencode off
Click Save
Verify settings.json ralph.providers.opencode.enabled is now false
Call ralph_providers MCP tool
Verify opencode no longer appears in providers list

description: Settings UI allows per-model allowed/blocked toggles
steps: Navigate to /settings/ralph
Uncheck 'Allowed' for haiku model under claude provider
Click Save
Verify settings.json ralph.providers.claude.models_allowed does NOT contain 'haiku'
Call ralph_providers MCP tool
Verify haiku is not in claude's models list

description: Settings UI allows cost tier selection per model
steps: Navigate to /settings/ralph
Select 'expensive' from cost tier dropdown for opus
Select 'moderate' for sonnet
Select 'cheap' for haiku
Click Save
Verify settings.json model_metadata has correct cost_tier values
Call ralph_providers
Verify each model returns its cost_tier in the response

description: Settings UI allows best-for tag selection with predefined tags and freeform notes
steps: Navigate to /settings/ralph
Select 'complex reasoning' and 'architecture' tags from multi-select for opus
Type 'Great for difficult refactoring tasks' in the notes field for opus
Click Save
Verify settings.json model_metadata.opus has best_for_tags=['complex reasoning', 'architecture']
Verify best_for_notes contains the freeform text
Call ralph_providers
Verify opus model returns both tags and notes

description: Settings UI defaults section has cascading provider/model dropdowns
steps: Navigate to /settings/ralph
Verify default provider dropdown shows enabled providers
Change default provider from 'claude' to 'opencode'
Verify default model dropdown updates to show opencode's models (live discovered)
Select a model, click Save
Verify settings.json ralph.defaults updated correctly

description: Settings UI summarizer section configuration
steps: Navigate to /settings/ralph
Verify summarizer provider and model dropdowns show current config
Change summarizer model from 'haiku' to 'sonnet'
Click Save
Verify settings.json ralph.summarizer.model is now 'sonnet'

description: Settings UI save preserves non-ralph settings
steps: Note current server and top-level providers sections in settings.json
Navigate to /settings/ralph and make changes
Click Save
Verify server section is unchanged in settings.json
Verify top-level providers section is unchanged

description: Settings UI GET /api/settings/ralph returns merged live + saved data
steps: GET /api/settings/ralph
Verify each provider has 'live_models' (from provider.get_models())
Verify each provider has 'models_allowed' and 'model_metadata' (from settings)
Verify 'available_tags' list is returned with predefined tag options

description: Settings UI PUT /api/settings/ralph saves configuration
steps: PUT /api/settings/ralph with updated ralph config
Verify 200 response
Read settings.json and verify ralph section updated
Verify other sections preserved

description: Settings UI handles provider CLI not installed
steps: Navigate to /settings/ralph with opencode CLI not installed
Verify opencode provider section shows empty model table
Verify warning message: 'CLI not found' or similar

description: Settings UI handles stale model metadata
steps: Configure model_metadata for a model that no longer exists in provider.get_models()
Navigate to /settings/ralph
Verify stale model appears grayed out with 'Not available' badge
Verify user can remove the stale entry

description: Settings UI Refresh Models button re-discovers without page reload
steps: Navigate to /settings/ralph
Click 'Refresh Models' button
Verify GET /api/settings/ralph/models is called
Verify model tables update with fresh live discovery results

description: Settings UI is accessible from dashboard navigation
steps: Open Vista dashboard
Verify settings/ralph link is visible in navigation sidebar
Click the link
Verify settings page loads correctly

description: Settings UI shows unsaved changes indicator
steps: Navigate to /settings/ralph
Make a change (e.g., toggle a model)
Verify Save button visually indicates unsaved changes (highlight, badge, etc.)
Click Save
Verify indicator clears after successful save
